world.title: Australia cracks down on student and backpacker visas to curb migration
world.summary: Australia will prohibit foreign students from bringing partners and children during their studies, according to a senior minister. Additionally, the government will tighten regulations for working holiday visas. These measures are part of a broader effort to address concerns regarding high migration levels, which have sparked increasing debate within the country. The changes aim to manage immigration more effectively.

world.title: Russia strikes Kyiv, other cities hours after US sanctions passed
world.summary: Russia launched missile and drone strikes on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities overnight, resulting in injuries to over two dozen individuals, according to officials. This attack occurred shortly after the U.S. Congress passed a significant sanctions bill aimed at Russia. The strikes mark a continued escalation in hostilities amid ongoing tensions between the two countries.

world.title: Aramco closes supply tap for Indian refiners, new oil barrels to cost more
world.summary: Saudi Arabia has ceased direct oil supply to Indian refiners, leading to increased costs for new barrels. Traders are expected to deliver limited volumes via the Strait of Hormuz, employing a strategy of purchasing discounted Iraqi crude. This crude will be transferred ship-to-ship in the Gulf of Oman before reaching Indian and other customers, maintaining recent trading practices.

business.title: Stocks in news: Infosys, Mazagon Dock, Fortis Healthcare, JSW Energy and Kalpataru Projects
business.summary: On September 16, Indian markets showed a cautious recovery, with the Nifty and Sensex rising after a significant drop the previous day. The Nifty 50 increased by 99 points, or 0.43%, closing at 23,217.60. Increased investments in banking and major stocks contributed to this rebound, while companies like Infosys and Mazagon Dock faced scrutiny due to recent corporate events.

business.title: Hospitals could be charging you 2,841% higher on commonly used consumables
business.summary: Hospitals in India are reportedly charging significantly higher prices for commonly used medical consumables. For example, an IV infusion set costs Rs 11 wholesale but has a maximum retail price of Rs 325, while a disposable syringe priced under Rs 7 is sold at a much higher rate. The Maharashtra FDA is revisiting the long-standing issue of medical device pricing.

business.title: Aramco closes supply tap for Indian refiners, new oil barrels to cost more
business.summary: Saudi Arabia has ceased direct oil supply to Indian refiners, leading to increased costs for new oil barrels. Traders are expected to deliver limited volumes through the Hormuz Strait, utilizing a strategy of purchasing discounted Iraqi crude. This crude is then transferred ship-to-ship in the Gulf of Oman for delivery to Indian and other customers.

technology.title: Apple iPhone Duo Max could rival Samsung Galaxy Z Fold Ultra
technology.summary: Apple is reportedly developing a larger foldable phone, potentially named the iPhone Duo Max, to compete with Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra. While the existing iPhone Duo directly rivals the Galaxy Z Fold 8, Apple currently lacks a comparable device to the Ultra model, which features a larger display and superior camera capabilities.

technology.title: Foxconn, Tata Electronics in overdrive for making iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max models for exports
technology.summary: Apple's iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max are being produced continuously in India by Foxconn and Tata Electronics. The factories are shipping the devices to the US and other global markets via chartered flights ahead of their launch on Friday. This marks the first time Made-in-India Pro iPhones will be available globally from day one.

technology.title: Google’s Gemini Notebook bundle of new features for more personalized powerful learning experience
technology.summary: Google's AI-powered research tool, Gemini Notebook, is set to introduce a new suite of features aimed at enhancing user experience. These updates will allow users to capture new sources and engage in chat functionalities with their notebooks. The rollout of these features is scheduled for the coming weeks, complementing and enhancing the existing capabilities of the tool.

sports.title: 'He is a God-gifted talent': Rashid Khan on Vaibhav Sooryavanshi - and the skill that is 'hardly' seen at such a young age | EXCLUSIVE
sports.summary: Rashid Khan praised young cricketer Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, calling him a "God-gifted talent" with exceptional skills rarely seen at such a young age. He noted the evolving dynamics of the India-Afghanistan rivalry, emphasizing that Afghanistan now possesses confidence and ambition, moving beyond merely hoping to compete against larger teams. This shift reflects a growing belief within the Afghan cricket team.

sports.title: Boehly, Walter sell Chelsea stakes as Clearlake takes full control
sports.summary: Clearlake Capital has acquired the ownership stakes of co-owners Todd Boehly and Mark Walter, gaining full control of Chelsea FC, the Premier League club announced on Wednesday. This transaction marks a significant shift in the club's ownership structure. Clearlake, led by Behdad Eghbali and Jose E. Feliciano, previously held a minority stake before this acquisition.

sports.title: Michael Carrick told he made huge mistake playing two 'inept' stars against Brighton
sports.summary: Manchester United's Carabao Cup defeat to Brighton has drawn criticism towards defenders Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven, who were described as 'inept' following their performances. United lost a two-goal lead, resulting in a 3-2 collapse at Old Trafford. The match ended with fans expressing their discontent through loud boos, highlighting the team's disappointing display.

health.title: J&J Slips as Caplyta Clears a Quality-of-Life Test
health.summary: Johnson & Johnson's Caplyta has shown promising late-stage data indicating improved sexual functioning in patients with depression, according to a Reuters report. This development may enhance Caplyta's commercial appeal. Despite this positive news, J&J's shares remained relatively stable, experiencing a slight decline. The findings could influence the drug's market position in the competitive pharmaceutical landscape.

health.title: Santiago Millan: What Will It Take to Make Cancer Medicines Accessible to Every Child?
health.summary: Santiago Millan, Technical Lead at the WHO's Global Platform for Access to Childhood Cancer Medicines, emphasized the need for equitable access to cancer treatments for all children. He discussed the barriers preventing access and called for collaborative efforts to ensure that no child is denied life-saving medications due to financial or logistical challenges in healthcare systems worldwide.

health.title: J&J Slips as Caplyta Clears a Quality-of-Life Test
health.summary: Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) experienced a decline in stock value following the release of late-stage data for Caplyta. The new findings indicate that Caplyta may enhance sexual functioning in patients with depression. This development adds a significant commercial argument for the drug, which is already positioned as a treatment option for individuals suffering from depressive disorders.

science.title: 15,000 years ago, enormous mammals like mammoths, large horse species dominated North America: How they went extinct
science.summary: Fifteen thousand years ago, North America was home to enormous mammals, including mammoths and large horse species, which dominated the landscape. This era featured a vastly different environment compared to today. The extinction of these species is attributed to various factors, including climate change and human activity, leading to significant ecological shifts and the eventual disappearance of these large mammals.

science.title: The Indian and Pacific Oceans Are Falling Out of Sync
science.summary: New research indicates a significant breakdown in the long-standing climate relationship between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Historically, climate changes in the Indian Ocean mirrored those in the Pacific for centuries. However, recent findings suggest that this synchronization is weakening, marking an unusual shift in climate patterns that could have implications for weather and environmental conditions in the region.

science.title: Onset of 55th eruptive episode at Kīlauea is still unknown, as 5 new vents have now opened in the crater
science.summary: Five new vents have opened on the northwest wall of Halemaʻumaʻu crater at Kīlauea, producing small lava flows, according to the Hawaiian Volcano Observatory. The summit region remains highly pressurized, but the onset of Kīlauea's 55th eruptive episode is still unknown. Forecasting future activity is not possible at this time, as conditions continue to evolve.
